description.narrative:
Founded in 1956, Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a well-established non-profit organisation currently operating in 40 countries.
DRC works to support refugees and displaced people, protect, and safeguard their rights and empowering them towards a better future, to realise DRC’s vision for a dignified life for all displaced. As a self-mandated protection agency, protection is at the core of DRC’s vision, mission, and operational and programmatic approach. Key commitments to a rights-based approach and adherence to the Humanitarian Principles underpin DRC’s work. DRC’s is working in five core sectors: Protection, Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), Shelter and Settlements, Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (HDP) and Economic Recovery.

Humanitära enheten kommer under 2022 att ge stöd till Danska flyktingkommittén (DRC). DRC grundades 1956 och är en väletablerad organisation som för närvarande arbetar i 40 länder. DRC arbetar med flyktingar och människor som befinner sig på flykt med fokus på skydd och rättigheter. Skyddsfrågan är kärnan i DRCs vision, uppdrag och operativa verksamhet. Rättighetsperspektivet och efterlevnad av de humanitära principerna ligger till grund för DRCs arbete. DRC:s arbetar inom dessa sektorer: skydd, bosättningar, humanitär nedrustning, fredsbyggande och ekonomisk återhämtning.

This contribution aims to support DRC in selected humanitarian crisis where DRC will implement specific projects and where the organisation has a clear added value to provide humanitarian assistance and protection to crisis affected populations. In most emergencies DRC works with a combination of two or more of the following sectors: • Protection • Shelter and Infrastructure • NFI distribution • Food security • WASH • Camp Management and Camp Coordination (CCCM) • Humanitarian Mine Action
Sida's humanitarian assistance to DRC 2025
Based on Sida's humanitarian needs based allocation process in late 2024, additional funds were added to DRC in 2025, which is the 4th year of the current multiyear Agreement. In October 2025, additional funds were added as part of the End of Year Allocation.
For 2025, the following support is proposed for DRC:
- Annual Projects/Programmes in line with Humanitarian Response Plans (usually 12 months) - 139 MSEK (where support to Yemen has been deducted and Cameroon and Ethiopia has been added in comparison to DRC's contextual portfolio for 2024. In October 2025, support was added to the Gaza crisis response)
- Rapid Response Mechanism- 15 MSEK (of which 5 MSEK were added as a top-up in October 2025)
- Method Development and Capacity Building- 4 MSEK
- End of agreement evaluation 650 000 SEK
Of note is that for 2025, the initial contribution to DRC in 2025 amounted to 492 750 000 SEK, with 146 650 000 SEK allocated in 2025. With the addition of 12 000 000 SEK as End of Year Allocation, the total contribution to DRC in 2025 amounts now to 504 750 000 SEK and for 2025, 158 650 000 SEK subject to Parliamentary appropriations.
Geographical support:
1. Burkina Faso PBA (10 MSEK): DRC has expertise in protection responses and leads the protection component of the RRM Frontline. Burkina Faso has been one of the pilot countries for the Sida funded Improved Access of the HardtoReach. DRC will focus on Boucle du Mouhoun and Nord regions in response to identified protection risks (including GBV) in partnership with local actors.
2. Cameroon (10 MSEK): In its initial submission for 2025 DRC requested 10 MSEK to provide timely and efficient multisectoral emergency response to newly displaced households in all seven divisions of the NW region many of which face significant access challenges and are hence underserved by aid actors, leaving gaps in food, protection, and shelter/NFI assistance through equitable partnerships with local civil society organisations based on strengthening their technical, organisational and operational capacities. DRC proposes to build the capacity of 6 selected CSOs in the NW (25 per cent of funds) and partner with up to two CSO:s to deliver emergency support for displacement response (55 per cent of funds), ensuring interventions are grounded in local knowledge and community trust. In 2024, DRC was the largest humanitarian NGO in Cameroon with 8.6 per cent of total funding.
3. Colombia (9 MSEK): DRC delivers integrated protection and emergency assistance responding to humanitarian needs of the crisis affected population in Nariño and Norte de Santander departments. DRC will provide immediate protection, legal and case management, basic needs assistance, while strengthening protective environments through community based interventions and awareness raising activities.
4. Ethiopia PBA (13 MSEK): DRC coleads the protection cluster, and plans to deliver protection centred and integrated multisectoral humanitarian assistance to refugees, IDPs returnees, and host communities affected by climate change and conflict, particularly in hardtoreach and underserved areas in Somali, Gambella, Afar, Tigray Regions and contested areas. DRC is one of four INGOs accredited in Ethiopia to work on humanitarian mine action, a key precondition for recovery. DRC serves as the administrative channel for Sidas support to the Humanitarian International NGO Forum (HINGO), which is a critical balance to the UN led Humanitarian Country Team (HCT). HINGO reinforces coordination and advocates on behalf of the NGO collective in Ethiopia on IHL, humanitarian principles and access.
5. Kenya PBA (5 MSEK): DRC will respond to humanitarian needs in refugee and hosting communities by providing emergency life saving needs in response to flooding and drought. DRC will provide support in Dadaab and Kakuma/ Kalobeyei as well as to the emergency preparedness and response to address the food security, WASH and protection needs of refugees and vulnerable persons in Garissa, Mandera, Wajir, Marsabit and Turkana counties where DRC is the leading protection actor. DRC has a s strong programmatic emphasis on protection in both refugee camps, marginalized and hard to reach areas, providing protection case management services in the refugee camps and working with community-based protection mechanisms to support at risk individuals and survivors of violence.
6. Myanmar (11 MSEK): DRC operations seek to improve community protection capacities, physical safety, psychosocial wellbeing and food security for conflict affected people through the delivery of multisectoral assistance. DRC operate in hardtoreach locations in Sagaing, Kachin, and Northern Shan State. The added value of DRC is its strong Protection focus in hardtoreach areas that incorporate elements of explosive ordnance risk education.
7. Somalia PBA (30 MSEK): DRC has been in the forefront of developing the humanitarian assistance regarding for example the integrated response framework, strengthening coordination efforts, and moving to vulnerability based targeting. Sida assess DRC to be a strong actor in Somalia and thus suggest to provide DRC Somalia with programme based funding in 2025. DRCs overall objective is to support vulnerable IDP households (HHs) and communities affected by conflict and natural disasters to meet lifesaving basic needs. Sectorial focus is put on CCCM, protection, WASH, shelter/NFI, emergency response and economic recovery. DRC works in various parts of the country, with a strong focus on areas identified as those with highest level of needs in the HNRP.
8. Sudan PBA (28 MSEK): DRC will implement its programme in Central Darfur, Khartoum, South Darfur, South Kordofan, Gedaref, White Nile, and Red Sea, states that have either been among the most conflict affected or that have been the destination of newly displaced persons. DRC has a protection centred approach and is working to ensure that people in hardtoreach areas also can receive protection, partly through local grassroots organisations. By putting protection at the centre and by having a clear ambition to reach areas affected by conflict, DRC is a relevant partner for Sidas humanitarian allocation to Sudan.
9. Ukraine (15 MSEK): DRC has a particular focus on hardtoreach areas where they seek to address the most acute basic needs and protection gaps though locally driven responses. Through their country program DRC, together with their partners, will facilitate improved access to services through tailored shelter solutions, cash assistance, legal advice, mobile protection support, psychosocial support and mine risk education.
10. Gaza (7 MSEK): Together with local partners, DRC will provide support to people in Gaza city as well as people en route southwards and in reception areas. The work will focus on distribution of basic needs items, improving living conditions in camps, and providing protection services such as psychosocial support and explosive ordnance risk education. Already working with the Gaza crisis response, DRC has communicated a need for additional funding in order to scale up the response for the remainder of 2025.
Rapid Response Mechanism: - RRM (15 MSEK): Part of the annual humanitarian budget is set aside for sudden humanitarian crises and deterioration of ongoing crises. For these situations, Sida has a Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) with partner organizations that makes it possible to fund lifesaving responses worldwide within 24 hours. DRC is applying for RRM funding which has both predisaster and postdisaster objectives. DRC has as growing experience in proactive humanitarian interventions and at the end of 2024 had nine ongoing proactive interventions ahead of conflict and climate related displacement. DRC has submitted its new Anticipatory Action (AA) Policy 20252030 and an Early Action Protocol Template.
Method and capacity building support
- Advancing Preventive and Responsive Capacity and Joint Action for Quality Protection Outcomes (4 MSEK): DRC aims to further advance and strengthen DRC's and local actors capacity to prevent and respond to protection risks that crisis affected people face, thereby strengthening protection outcomes for crisis affected people at risk of violence, coercion, and deliberate deprivation.
Evaluation
- End of agreement evaluation (650 000 SEK): as 2025 is the final year for DRC's multiyear agreement, an end of agreement evaluation will be conducted to assess the overall achievements will be carried out.
